name: Tuna pasta bake
summary: Penne, tinned tuna and sweetcorn folded through a cheesy white sauce and baked until bubbling and golden on top, a cupboard-staple family dinner.
about: Made from what is already in the cupboard, tuna pasta bake is one of the weeknight dinners South African families come back to most. It stretches a few tins to feed a crowd and reheats well for lunch the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and grease a large ovenproof dish, about 30 × 20 cm.
Cook the penne in a big pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, so it is still firm in the middle. Drain.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and fry the onion until soft but not brown, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the milk a little at a time, whisking constantly. Simmer, still whisking, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in three-quarters of the cheese, the mustard powder, salt and pepper until the cheese has melted.
Fold in the pasta, tuna, sweetcorn and peas and spoon everything into the dish. Scatter the rest of the cheese over the top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling at the edges and the cheese is golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
prepNote: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate; bake from cold for 35 to 40 minutes.
